title: Welcome to English class
grammar: Verb be: affirmative and negative; Subject pronouns
pair_game: Act a greeting with your hands. Your partner says the words. Then swap!

grammar_box.title: Verb be
rows: I’m not late. He isn’t sad.
grammar_box.tip: Short forms: I am → I’m, you are → you’re, he is → he’s (qisqa shakllar)

questions: What is your name? How do you spell it?
Where are you from? Are you from Uzbekistan?
How old are you? Are you a student?
What is your teacher's name? Is she/he nice?
Are you happy in English class? Why or why not?
Who is your best friend? Is he or she in your class?
What is your favorite greeting in English? Do you use it every day?
Are you good at English? What is easy and what is difficult for you?
How do you say hello and goodbye to your friends in Uzbekistan?
Is English class interesting for you? What do you like about it?
starters: I’m from … . Yes, I am. / No, I’m not.
I’m … years old. Yes, I’m a …
My teacher’s name is … . She’s / He’s …
Yes, I am. / No, I’m not. Because …
My best friend is … . He’s / She’s in …
My favourite greeting is … . Yes, I … / No, I …
I’m good at … . … is easy. … is difficult.
We say … for hello and … for goodbye.
Yes, it is. / No, it isn’t. I like …
samples: What is your name? How do you spell it?
Where are you from? Are you from Uzbekistan?
**I’m from** Samarkand. Yes, **I am** from Uzbekistan!
How do you say hello and goodbye to your friends in Uzbekistan?
We say **“Assalomu alaykum”** for hello. For goodbye we say **“Xayr”**.

game.title: Find someone who…
game.rules: Walk around the class. Ask: “Are you …?” Write a name.
items: … is a big brother or sister

mini_talk.title: All about me
mini_talk.model: Hello! **I’m** Bobur. My name is spelled B-O-B-U-R. **I’m** eleven years old. **I’m** from Samarkand in Uzbekistan. **I’m** a student. My teacher **is** very nice. My best friend **is** Ali. He **is** in my class. **We are** happy in English class. Goodbye! See you later!
